## Corporate relocations driving some growth
A significant number of corporate relocations have come out of states such as California, Illinois, and New York. These massive site selection projects create an opportunity for employees to relocate to lower-cost geographies with lower taxes, less expensive housing, and more attractive quality of life among other traditional site selection factors. These projects include headquarters, manufacturing plants, distribution centers, call centers, and other similar operations. Some recent examples include:
*   McKesson from San Francisco to Dallas  
*   Caterpiller from Chicago to Dallas  
*   AECOM from Los Angeles to Dallas  
*   Digital Realty from San Francisco to Austin, Texas  
*   Oracle from Silicon Valley to Austin, Texas  
*   Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE), a spinoff from San Francisco’s HP, to Houston  
*   Norfolk Southern from Norfolk, Virginia, to Atlanta

## Population growth data identifies the winners and losers
COVID amplified the demographic shifts occurring in the U.S. By analyzing the population changes from 2019 to 2022, you are able to identify the winning and losing cities across the U.S.
There are really two ways to analyze the data. The first option is to evaluate the net new population growth and the other is to analyze the percentage growth. The net new population growth approach will benefit the large metro areas as they have a larger base population to grow from, which means that even a small percentage growth can equate to a large net new population increase. Conversely, if you calculate the percentage growth rate, smaller metro areas will emerge as it is much easier to grow rapidly if starting from a smaller base population.

## Corporate relocations driving some growth
A significant number of corporate relocations have come out of states such as California, Illinois, and New York. These massive site selection projects create an opportunity for employees to relocate to lower-cost geographies with lower taxes, less expensive housing, and more attractive quality of life among other traditional site selection factors. These projects include headquarters, manufacturing plants, distribution centers, call centers, and other similar operations. Some recent examples include:
*   McKesson from San Francisco to Dallas  
*   Caterpiller from Chicago to Dallas  
*   AECOM from Los Angeles to Dallas  
*   Digital Realty from San Francisco to Austin, Texas  
*   Oracle from Silicon Valley to Austin, Texas  
*   Hewlett-Packard Enterprise (HPE), a spinoff from San Francisco’s HP, to Houston  
*   Norfolk Southern from Norfolk, Virginia, to Atlanta

## Population growth data identifies the winners and losers
COVID amplified the demographic shifts occurring in the U.S. By analyzing the population changes from 2019 to 2022, you are able to identify the winning and losing cities across the U.S.
There are really two ways to analyze the data. The first option is to evaluate the net new population growth and the other is to analyze the percentage growth. The net new population growth approach will benefit the large metro areas as they have a larger base population to grow from, which means that even a small percentage growth can equate to a large net new population increase. Conversely, if you calculate the percentage growth rate, smaller metro areas will emerge as it is much easier to grow rapidly if starting from a smaller base population.

**Raja Ravi Varma** (Malayalam:[[ɾaːd͡ʒaː ɾɐʋi ʋɐrmːɐ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam")) (29 April 1848 – 2 October 1906[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-4)) was an Indian painter. His works are one of the best examples of the fusion of European [academic art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academic_art "Academic art") with a purely Indian sensibility and iconography. He greatly enhanced his reach and influence as a painter and public figure by making affordable [lithographs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithography "Lithography") of his paintings available to the public. His lithographs increased the involvement of common people with fine arts and defined artistic tastes. His religious depictions of Hindu deities and works from [Indian epic poetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_epic_poetry "Indian epic poetry") and [Puranas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puranas "Puranas") have received critical acclaim. He was part of the royal family of [Parappanad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parappanad "Parappanad"), [Malappuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malappuram_district "Malappuram district").
Raja Ravi Varma was closely related to the royal family of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") of present-day [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala") state in India. Later in his life, two of his granddaughters were adopted into the royal family.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-5)

Varma was born on 29 April 1848, as [M. R. Ry.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maha_Raja_Rajya_Shri "Maha Raja Rajya Shri") Ravi Varma ([Malayalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malayalam_language "Malayalam language"): രവി വർമ്മ), [Koil Thampuran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koyi_Thampuran "Koyi Thampuran") of Kilimanoor at [Kilimanoor palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilimanoor_palace "Kilimanoor palace") in the erstwhile [princely state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Princely_state "Princely state") of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") (present-day [Kerala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"))[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-pal-6) into an aristocratic family that for over 200 years produced consorts for the princesses of the matrilineal Travancore royal family. The title [Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja "Raja") was conferred as a personal title by the Viceroy and Governor-General of India [Lord Curzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lord_Curzon "Lord Curzon").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-pal-6)
[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/Raja_Ravi_Varma%2C_There_Comes_Papa_%281893%29.jpg/250px-Raja_Ravi_Varma%2C_There_Comes_Papa_%281893%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raja_Ravi_Varma,_There_Comes_Papa_(1893).jpg)

[_There comes Papa_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/There_Comes_Papa "There Comes Papa") (1893), depicting Varma's daughter Mahaprabha with one of her sons
[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_%281848%E2%80%931901%29.jpg/250px-Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_%281848%E2%80%931901%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_(1848%E2%80%931901).jpg)
Varma's sister-in-law, [Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi "Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi"), Senior Rani of [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal") (or [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Travancore "Kingdom of Travancore")), who adopted Varma's granddaughters in 1900

Ravi Varma was the son of Ezhumavil Neelakanthan Bhattatiripad and Uma Ambabayi Thampurratti. His mother Uma Ambabayi Thampuratty belonged to the baronial family which ruled the Kilimanoor [feudal estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fief "Fief") within the kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). She was a poet and writer, and her work _Parvati Swayamvaram_ was published by Varma after her death. Ravi Varma's father was a scholar of [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit") and [Ayurveda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayurveda "Ayurveda") and hailed from the [Ernakulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernakulam "Ernakulam") district in Kerala. Ravi Varma had two siblings, a sister named [Mangala Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangala_Bayi "Mangala Bayi") and a brother named [Raja Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._Raja_Raja_Varma "C. Raja Raja Varma") (born 1860). The last-named was also a painter and worked closely with Ravi Varma all his life.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1866, at age 18, Varma was married to 12-year-old Bhageerthi Bayi (known formally as Pooruruttati Nal Bhageerathi Bayi Thampuratty) of the royal house of [Mavelikkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mavelikkara "Mavelikkara"), another major [fief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fief "Fief") of Travancore kingdom. Notably, the house of Mavellikara was a branch of the Royal House of Travancore. Bhageerthi was the youngest of three sisters; her two elder siblings were adopted into the royal family of Travancore in 1857 to perpetuate the lineage. Designated the Senior and Junior Rani of Attingal, their descendants were vested with the succession to the throne of Travancore. Therefore, Ravi Varma's connection to the royal family became very close due to his marriage with Bhageerthi. His children would be royal by birth, since they belonged to their mother's family. The marriage, which was arranged by the parents in the proper Indian manner, was considered successful. The couple had five children, two sons, and three daughters. Their elder son, Kerala Varma (b.1876) was of an excessively spiritual temperament. He never married and eventually renounced the world, leaving home for good in 1912. The younger son, Rama Varma (born 1879), inherited his father's artistic talent and studied at the [JJ School of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JJ_School_of_Arts "JJ School of Arts"), [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"). He was married to Gowri Kunjamma, sister of [Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewan "Dewan")[PGN Unnithan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGN_Unnithan "PGN Unnithan"), and became the father of seven children.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

He was followed by a brother (the future Maharaja [Marthanda Varma III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uthradom_Thirunal_Marthanda_Varma "Uthradom Thirunal Marthanda Varma")) and a sister [Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karthika_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi "Karthika Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi"), the mother of Maharaja [Rama Varma VII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moolam_Thirunal_Rama_Varma "Moolam Thirunal Rama Varma") who is presently on the throne (since 2013). Meanwhile, the Senior Rani ([Sethu Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sethu_Lakshmi_Bayi "Sethu Lakshmi Bayi"), daughter of Mahaprabha Amma, and Regent from 1924 to 1931) also gave birth to two daughters later in life (in 1923 and 1926).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
In this way, the entire present (existing) royal family of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") is descended from Raja Ravi Varma. Well known among his royal descendants are the writers [Aswathi Thirunal Gowri Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aswathi_Thirunal_Gowri_Lakshmi_Bayi "Aswathi Thirunal Gowri Lakshmi Bayi") and [Shreekumar Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreekumar_Varma "Shreekumar Varma"), the artist [Rukmini Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rukmini_Varma "Rukmini Varma") and the classical musician [Aswathi Thirunal Rama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aswathi_Thirunal_Rama_Varma "Aswathi Thirunal Rama Varma").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Around Ravi Varma's 57th birthday he announced his decision to accept [Sanyasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanyasa "Sanyasa"), and retire from all worldly life when he turned 60. In his final years he suffered from grief for the death of Raja Raja Varma, and also from diabetes, which contributed to his death on 2 October 1906.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
Varma was patronised by [Ayilyam Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayilyam_Thirunal "Ayilyam Thirunal"), the next [Maharaja of Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja_of_Travancore "Maharaja of Travancore") and began formal training thereafter.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-The_Diary_of_C._Rajaraja_Varma-7) He learned the basics of painting in [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai "Madurai"). Later, he was trained in water painting by Rama Swami Naidu and rather reluctantly in [oil painting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_painting "Oil painting") by British portraitist Theodore Jenson.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-8)
[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg/250px-Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg)
The studio used by Varma during his stay at the [Laxmi Vilas Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmi_Vilas_Palace "Laxmi Vilas Palace")

The British administrator, [Edgar Thurston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Thurston "Edgar Thurston") was significant in promoting the careers of Varma and his brother.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-9) Varma received widespread acclaim after he won an award for an exhibition of his paintings at Vienna in 1873. Varma's paintings were also sent to the [World's Columbian Exposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_Columbian_Exposition "World's Columbian Exposition") held in Chicago in 1893 and he was awarded three gold medals.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-10) He travelled throughout India in search of subjects. He often modelled Hindu [Goddesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goddess "Goddess") on [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_India "South India") women, whom he considered beautiful. Ravi Varma is particularly noted for his paintings depicting episodes from the story of [Dushyanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dushyanta "Dushyanta") and [Shakuntala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakuntala "Shakuntala"), and [Nala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nala "Nala") and [Damayanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damayanti "Damayanti"), from the [Mahabharata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahabharata "Mahabharata"). Ravi Varma's representation of [Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu "Hindu") characters has become a part of the Indian imagination of the epics. He is often criticized for being too showy and sentimental in his style but his work remains very popular in India. Many of his fabulous paintings are housed at [Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmi_Vilas_Palace,_Vadodara "Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-11)

Title: 15 Things You Need To Know About Raja Ravi Varma
Chunks: 0,1,2,3,4
Bringing detail and realism to Indian imagery with a delicate interplay of light and shadows, Raja Ravi Varma is known for his stunning canvasses that have influenced generations of Indian artists.
![Image 1](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Ravi-Varma-Blog-New-Facebook-Size_grande.jpg?v=1473312021)
![Image 2](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Ravivarma1_large.png?v=1473312277)_(A photograph of Raja Ravi Varma taken in the 1890's)_
Though a protégé of royalty who was known for his portraits of Kings, Queens and Aristocrats, Raja Ravi Varma was also the first to make lithographs of his artworks affordable and easily available, bringing fine art to the masses.
![Image 3](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_Ravi_Varma__Maharaja_Sayaji_Rao_grande.jpg?v=1473312559)_(Portrait of Maharaja Sayaji Rao of Baroda by Raja Ravi Varma)_
The first to use European realism and art techniques with Indian subjects, his portrayal of Indian Gods and mythological characters shaped Indian “calendar art”, and greatly influenced Indian literature and the film industry!
[![Image 4](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/11_Artisera_Fine-art_Lithographs_Ravi-varma-press_Laxmi_1_grande.jpg?v=1473312796)](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)[_(An oleograph by Raja Ravi Varma depicting the Goddess, Laxmi; click to purchase on Artisera)_](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)
**Here are 15 interesting facts about Raja Ravi Varma that you must know.**

1. Ravi Varma was born in 1848 in Kilimanoor, Kerala into a family of scholars, poets and artists. His mother's family followed the matrilineal system of lineage and succession. Therefore, Ravi Varma belonged to the family of his mother, and his children belonged to the family of their mother.
![Image 5](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Studiorrv_grande.jpg?v=1473313011)_(Birthplace of Raja Ravi Varma with his studio in the foreground)_
2. When Ravi Varma was a young boy, his uncle recognized his artistic talent, and sent him to the then ruling king, Ayilyam Thirunal, who helped him receive an education in arts, exposed him to western styles of painting, and had him trained by the palace painter.
![Image 6](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_ravivarma_painting_50_historic_meeting_grande.jpg?v=1473313083)_(Painting by Raja Ravi Varma depicting the 3rd Duke of Buckingham being greeted by Maharaja Ayilyam Thirunal and Visakham Thirunal of Travancore)_
3. At the age of 18, Varma married 12-year-old Bhageerthi Bayi of the royal house of Mavelikkara. The couple were blessed with two sons and three daughters. One of his daughters, Mahaprabha Amma, features in some of his most famous paintings.
![Image 7](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_Ravi_Varma__There_Comes_Papa__1893_grande.jpg?v=1473313330)_(A painting by Ravi Varma of his daughter Mahaprabha Amma, with one of her sons)_

4. In 1904, Viceroy Lord Curzon, on behalf of the British Emperor, bestowed upon Varma, the Kaisar-i-Hind Gold Medal. The citation for this award mentioned the title 'Raja' for the first time against his name. Varma then continued to use this title much to the consternation of the then Maharaja of Travancore, Sri Moolam Thirunal.
![Image 8](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/IMG_2524_grande.JPG?v=1473313448)_(The Kaisar-i-Hind Gold Medal. Image souce: british-medals.co.uk)_
5. The fame of Raja Ravi Varma reached to such great heights, that the small town of Kilimanoor, Varma’s birthplace, had to open a post office, as letters and requests for paintings came flooding in for him from various corners of the country!
![Image 9](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_Ravi_Varma__Galaxy_of_Musicians_grande.jpg?v=1473313597)_('Galaxy of Musicians', one of Raja Ravi Varma's most famous works)_
6. During his time, oil painting was a new medium, and it was only artist Ramaswamy Naicker of Madurai who had the knowledge of oil painting techniques. Seeing Raja Ravi Varma as a potential rival, Naicker refused to teach him the technique. It was Arumugham Pillai, Naicker's student, who taught Varma the nuances of oil painting, sneaking into the latter’s house at night, much against the wishes of his teacher.
![Image 10](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja-Ravi-Varma-Paintings_2_grande.jpg?v=1473316850)_(Two of Ravi Varma's popular works: Left - Woman Holding a Fruit; Right - Scene from Kalidasa's 'The Recognition of Sakuntala')_

7. Raja Ravi Varma started a lithographic printing press in 1894, which was eventually sold to a printing technician from Germany. The oleographs produced by the press, mainly depicting gods, goddesses, and scenes from Mahabharata, Ramayana and Puranas, were very popular and continued to be printed in thousands, for many years.
![Image 11](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/varma06_grande.jpg?v=1473313850)_(Some of Varma's paintings along with the lithography stones used in the press, at the Raja Ravi Varma Archival Museum, Manipal. Image source:indiaheritagevillage.org)_
![Image 12](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Artisera_Raja_Ravi_Varma_Jatayu_Vadham_grande.jpg?v=1473325623)_(Ravi Varma's 'Jatayu Vadham', depicting a scene from the Ramayana)_
8. In the early 20 th century, women from Chettinad, a region in Tamil Nadu, began decorating Ravi Varma’s lithographs with zardozi embroidery and glitter work. These embellished prints included those from the Ravi Varma press and other presses, and can be dated from early to mid 20th century.
[![Image 13](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/13_Artisera_Fine-art_Oleograph_7395_1_1024x1024_grande.jpg?v=1473314821)](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)[_(An embellished oleograph with zari and textile, depicting the 'Shiv Parivaar'; click to purchase on Artisera)_](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)

9. Raja Ravi Varma’s brother, C. Raja Raja Varma was an accomplished landscape artist. Most information about the life of Raja Ravi Varma is through ‘_The Diary of C. Raja Raja Varma_’, written by his brother, who was also Varma’s assistant and business manager.
![Image 14](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja-Ravi-Varma-Paintings_1_12f12238-5113-4682-a116-b6cd5adb07b6_grande.jpg?v=1473317489)_(Left: Portrait of C. Raja Raja Varma; Right: The Diary of C. Raja Raja Varma)_
10. Raja Ravi Varma was specially commissioned by the Maharaja of Vadodara to create portraits of the royal family and paintings based on Hindu mythology. A large collection of these is still displayed at the Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara.
![Image 15](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/562137_grande.jpg?v=1473315152)_(The Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara. Image Source: wall.alphacoders.com)_
![Image 16](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Chinmabai_grande.jpg?v=1473315229)_(Portrait of Maharani Chimnabai of Baroda by Raja Ravi Varma)_
11. In 2013, a crater on Mercury was named ‘Varma’ in his honour!

12. Two of Ravi Varma’s granddaughters were adopted into the royal family of Travancore, and their descendants comprise the royal family, including the present titular Maharajah of Travancore, Rama Varma VII, who ascended the throne in 2013.

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/Raja_Ravi_Varma%2C_There_Comes_Papa_%281893%29.jpg/250px-Raja_Ravi_Varma%2C_There_Comes_Papa_%281893%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raja_Ravi_Varma,_There_Comes_Papa_(1893).jpg)
texts.4:
[_There comes Papa_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/There_Comes_Papa "There Comes Papa") (1893), depicting Varma's daughter Mahaprabha with one of her sons
[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_%281848%E2%80%931901%29.jpg/250px-Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_%281848%E2%80%931901%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rani_Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi_of_Travancore_(1848%E2%80%931901).jpg)
Varma's sister-in-law, [Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharani_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi "Bharani Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi"), Senior Rani of [Attingal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attingal "Attingal") (or [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Travancore "Kingdom of Travancore")), who adopted Varma's granddaughters in 1900
texts.5: Ravi Varma was the son of Ezhumavil Neelakanthan Bhattatiripad and Uma Ambabayi Thampurratti. His mother Uma Ambabayi Thampuratty belonged to the baronial family which ruled the Kilimanoor [feudal estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fief "Fief") within the kingdom of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore"). She was a poet and writer, and her work _Parvati Swayamvaram_ was published by Varma after her death. Ravi Varma's father was a scholar of [Sanskrit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanskrit "Sanskrit") and [Ayurveda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayurveda "Ayurveda") and hailed from the [Ernakulam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernakulam "Ernakulam") district in Kerala. Ravi Varma had two siblings, a sister named [Mangala Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mangala_Bayi "Mangala Bayi") and a brother named [Raja Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._Raja_Raja_Varma "C. Raja Raja Varma") (born 1860). The last-named was also a painter and worked closely with Ravi Varma all his life.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
texts.6: In 1866, at age 18, Varma was married to 12-year-old Bhageerthi Bayi (known formally as Pooruruttati Nal Bhageerathi Bayi Thampuratty) of the royal house of [Mavelikkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mavelikkara "Mavelikkara"), another major [fief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fief "Fief") of Travancore kingdom. Notably, the house of Mavellikara was a branch of the Royal House of Travancore. Bhageerthi was the youngest of three sisters; her two elder siblings were adopted into the royal family of Travancore in 1857 to perpetuate the lineage. Designated the Senior and Junior Rani of Attingal, their descendants were vested with the succession to the throne of Travancore. Therefore, Ravi Varma's connection to the royal family became very close due to his marriage with Bhageerthi. His children would be royal by birth, since they belonged to their mother's family. The marriage, which was arranged by the parents in the proper Indian manner, was considered successful. The couple had five children, two sons, and three daughters. Their elder son, Kerala Varma (b.1876) was of an excessively spiritual temperament. He never married and eventually renounced the world, leaving home for good in 1912. The younger son, Rama Varma (born 1879), inherited his father's artistic talent and studied at the [JJ School of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JJ_School_of_Arts "JJ School of Arts"), [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"). He was married to Gowri Kunjamma, sister of [Dewan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dewan "Dewan")[PGN Unnithan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PGN_Unnithan "PGN Unnithan"), and became the father of seven children.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
texts.9:
He was followed by a brother (the future Maharaja [Marthanda Varma III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uthradom_Thirunal_Marthanda_Varma "Uthradom Thirunal Marthanda Varma")) and a sister [Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karthika_Thirunal_Lakshmi_Bayi "Karthika Thirunal Lakshmi Bayi"), the mother of Maharaja [Rama Varma VII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moolam_Thirunal_Rama_Varma "Moolam Thirunal Rama Varma") who is presently on the throne (since 2013). Meanwhile, the Senior Rani ([Sethu Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sethu_Lakshmi_Bayi "Sethu Lakshmi Bayi"), daughter of Mahaprabha Amma, and Regent from 1924 to 1931) also gave birth to two daughters later in life (in 1923 and 1926).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
In this way, the entire present (existing) royal family of [Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore "Travancore") is descended from Raja Ravi Varma. Well known among his royal descendants are the writers [Aswathi Thirunal Gowri Lakshmi Bayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aswathi_Thirunal_Gowri_Lakshmi_Bayi "Aswathi Thirunal Gowri Lakshmi Bayi") and [Shreekumar Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shreekumar_Varma "Shreekumar Varma"), the artist [Rukmini Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rukmini_Varma "Rukmini Varma") and the classical musician [Aswathi Thirunal Rama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aswathi_Thirunal_Rama_Varma "Aswathi Thirunal Rama Varma").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
texts.10:
Around Ravi Varma's 57th birthday he announced his decision to accept [Sanyasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanyasa "Sanyasa"), and retire from all worldly life when he turned 60. In his final years he suffered from grief for the death of Raja Raja Varma, and also from diabetes, which contributed to his death on 2 October 1906.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
Varma was patronised by [Ayilyam Thirunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayilyam_Thirunal "Ayilyam Thirunal"), the next [Maharaja of Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja_of_Travancore "Maharaja of Travancore") and began formal training thereafter.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-The_Diary_of_C._Rajaraja_Varma-7) He learned the basics of painting in [Madurai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madurai "Madurai"). Later, he was trained in water painting by Rama Swami Naidu and rather reluctantly in [oil painting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_painting "Oil painting") by British portraitist Theodore Jenson.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-8)
[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/87/Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg/250px-Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Raja_Ravi_Verma_Studio_Vadodara.jpg)
The studio used by Varma during his stay at the [Laxmi Vilas Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmi_Vilas_Palace "Laxmi Vilas Palace")
texts.11: The British administrator, [Edgar Thurston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edgar_Thurston "Edgar Thurston") was significant in promoting the careers of Varma and his brother.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-9) Varma received widespread acclaim after he won an award for an exhibition of his paintings at Vienna in 1873. Varma's paintings were also sent to the [World's Columbian Exposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_Columbian_Exposition "World's Columbian Exposition") held in Chicago in 1893 and he was awarded three gold medals.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-10) He travelled throughout India in search of subjects. He often modelled Hindu [Goddesses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goddess "Goddess") on [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_India "South India") women, whom he considered beautiful. Ravi Varma is particularly noted for his paintings depicting episodes from the story of [Dushyanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dushyanta "Dushyanta") and [Shakuntala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakuntala "Shakuntala"), and [Nala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nala "Nala") and [Damayanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damayanti "Damayanti"), from the [Mahabharata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahabharata "Mahabharata"). Ravi Varma's representation of [Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu "Hindu") characters has become a part of the Indian imagination of the epics. He is often criticized for being too showy and sentimental in his style but his work remains very popular in India. Many of his fabulous paintings are housed at [Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laxmi_Vilas_Palace,_Vadodara "Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Ravi_Varma#cite_note-11)

texts.0:
Bringing detail and realism to Indian imagery with a delicate interplay of light and shadows, Raja Ravi Varma is known for his stunning canvasses that have influenced generations of Indian artists.
![Image 1](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Ravi-Varma-Blog-New-Facebook-Size_grande.jpg?v=1473312021)
![Image 2](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Ravivarma1_large.png?v=1473312277)_(A photograph of Raja Ravi Varma taken in the 1890's)_
Though a protégé of royalty who was known for his portraits of Kings, Queens and Aristocrats, Raja Ravi Varma was also the first to make lithographs of his artworks affordable and easily available, bringing fine art to the masses.
![Image 3](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_Ravi_Varma__Maharaja_Sayaji_Rao_grande.jpg?v=1473312559)_(Portrait of Maharaja Sayaji Rao of Baroda by Raja Ravi Varma)_
The first to use European realism and art techniques with Indian subjects, his portrayal of Indian Gods and mythological characters shaped Indian “calendar art”, and greatly influenced Indian literature and the film industry!
[![Image 4](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/11_Artisera_Fine-art_Lithographs_Ravi-varma-press_Laxmi_1_grande.jpg?v=1473312796)](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)[_(An oleograph by Raja Ravi Varma depicting the Goddess, Laxmi; click to purchase on Artisera)_](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)
**Here are 15 interesting facts about Raja Ravi Varma that you must know.**
texts.1:
1. Ravi Varma was born in 1848 in Kilimanoor, Kerala into a family of scholars, poets and artists. His mother's family followed the matrilineal system of lineage and succession. Therefore, Ravi Varma belonged to the family of his mother, and his children belonged to the family of their mother.
![Image 5](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Studiorrv_grande.jpg?v=1473313011)_(Birthplace of Raja Ravi Varma with his studio in the foreground)_
2. When Ravi Varma was a young boy, his uncle recognized his artistic talent, and sent him to the then ruling king, Ayilyam Thirunal, who helped him receive an education in arts, exposed him to western styles of painting, and had him trained by the palace painter.
![Image 6](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_ravivarma_painting_50_historic_meeting_grande.jpg?v=1473313083)_(Painting by Raja Ravi Varma depicting the 3rd Duke of Buckingham being greeted by Maharaja Ayilyam Thirunal and Visakham Thirunal of Travancore)_
3. At the age of 18, Varma married 12-year-old Bhageerthi Bayi of the royal house of Mavelikkara. The couple were blessed with two sons and three daughters. One of his daughters, Mahaprabha Amma, features in some of his most famous paintings.
![Image 7](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_Ravi_Varma__There_Comes_Papa__1893_grande.jpg?v=1473313330)_(A painting by Ravi Varma of his daughter Mahaprabha Amma, with one of her sons)_
texts.2:
4. In 1904, Viceroy Lord Curzon, on behalf of the British Emperor, bestowed upon Varma, the Kaisar-i-Hind Gold Medal. The citation for this award mentioned the title 'Raja' for the first time against his name. Varma then continued to use this title much to the consternation of the then Maharaja of Travancore, Sri Moolam Thirunal.
![Image 8](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/IMG_2524_grande.JPG?v=1473313448)_(The Kaisar-i-Hind Gold Medal. Image souce: british-medals.co.uk)_
5. The fame of Raja Ravi Varma reached to such great heights, that the small town of Kilimanoor, Varma’s birthplace, had to open a post office, as letters and requests for paintings came flooding in for him from various corners of the country!
![Image 9](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja_Ravi_Varma__Galaxy_of_Musicians_grande.jpg?v=1473313597)_('Galaxy of Musicians', one of Raja Ravi Varma's most famous works)_
6. During his time, oil painting was a new medium, and it was only artist Ramaswamy Naicker of Madurai who had the knowledge of oil painting techniques. Seeing Raja Ravi Varma as a potential rival, Naicker refused to teach him the technique. It was Arumugham Pillai, Naicker's student, who taught Varma the nuances of oil painting, sneaking into the latter’s house at night, much against the wishes of his teacher.
![Image 10](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja-Ravi-Varma-Paintings_2_grande.jpg?v=1473316850)_(Two of Ravi Varma's popular works: Left - Woman Holding a Fruit; Right - Scene from Kalidasa's 'The Recognition of Sakuntala')_
texts.3:
7. Raja Ravi Varma started a lithographic printing press in 1894, which was eventually sold to a printing technician from Germany. The oleographs produced by the press, mainly depicting gods, goddesses, and scenes from Mahabharata, Ramayana and Puranas, were very popular and continued to be printed in thousands, for many years.
![Image 11](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/varma06_grande.jpg?v=1473313850)_(Some of Varma's paintings along with the lithography stones used in the press, at the Raja Ravi Varma Archival Museum, Manipal. Image source:indiaheritagevillage.org)_
![Image 12](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Artisera_Raja_Ravi_Varma_Jatayu_Vadham_grande.jpg?v=1473325623)_(Ravi Varma's 'Jatayu Vadham', depicting a scene from the Ramayana)_
8. In the early 20 th century, women from Chettinad, a region in Tamil Nadu, began decorating Ravi Varma’s lithographs with zardozi embroidery and glitter work. These embellished prints included those from the Ravi Varma press and other presses, and can be dated from early to mid 20th century.
[![Image 13](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/13_Artisera_Fine-art_Oleograph_7395_1_1024x1024_grande.jpg?v=1473314821)](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)[_(An embellished oleograph with zari and textile, depicting the 'Shiv Parivaar'; click to purchase on Artisera)_](http://www.artisera.com/collections/raja-ravi-varma)
texts.4:
9. Raja Ravi Varma’s brother, C. Raja Raja Varma was an accomplished landscape artist. Most information about the life of Raja Ravi Varma is through ‘_The Diary of C. Raja Raja Varma_’, written by his brother, who was also Varma’s assistant and business manager.
![Image 14](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Raja-Ravi-Varma-Paintings_1_12f12238-5113-4682-a116-b6cd5adb07b6_grande.jpg?v=1473317489)_(Left: Portrait of C. Raja Raja Varma; Right: The Diary of C. Raja Raja Varma)_
10. Raja Ravi Varma was specially commissioned by the Maharaja of Vadodara to create portraits of the royal family and paintings based on Hindu mythology. A large collection of these is still displayed at the Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara.
![Image 15](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/562137_grande.jpg?v=1473315152)_(The Laxmi Vilas Palace, Vadodara. Image Source: wall.alphacoders.com)_
![Image 16](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0849/4704/files/Chinmabai_grande.jpg?v=1473315229)_(Portrait of Maharani Chimnabai of Baroda by Raja Ravi Varma)_
11. In 2013, a crater on Mercury was named ‘Varma’ in his honour!

12. Two of Ravi Varma’s granddaughters were adopted into the royal family of Travancore, and their descendants comprise the royal family, including the present titular Maharajah of Travancore, Rama Varma VII, who ascended the throne in 2013.

**[Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") Parliamentary (Lok Sabha) Constituency** is one of the 20 parliamentary constituencies in Kerala, India. It is located in [Thiruvananthapuram district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_district "Thiruvananthapuram district") and encompasses the major part of [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram") city, the capital of [Kerala State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala").

The incumbent MP of this constituency, [Shashi Tharoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Tharoor "Shashi Tharoor") of the [Indian National Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_National_Congress "Indian National Congress"), has been elected on 4 consecutive occasions: 2009, 2014, 2019 and 2024. He is the longest serving Member of Parliament to have represented the constituency.
This constituency is dominated By [Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") and [Nadar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-2) As per the electoral roll for the 2024 polls, the total electorate is of 14,03,281 people including 7,27,469 women, 6,75,771 men and 41 transgender people.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-3) Out of total electorate, 26% is rural and 74% is urban.

The Scheduled castes (SC) and Scheduled tribes (ST) is 9.82% and 0.45%, respectively of total electorate.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-4) The constituency also has highest proportion of [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") and [Converted Christians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conversion_to_Christianity "Conversion to Christianity") in Kerala.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-5)[Nairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nair "Nair") dominates the urban segments of [Kazhakootam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazhakootam_Assembly_constituency "Kazhakootam Assembly constituency"),[Nemom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemom_Assembly_constituency "Nemom Assembly constituency"),[Vattiyoorkavu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vattiyoorkavu_Assembly_constituency "Vattiyoorkavu Assembly constituency") and [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Assembly_constituency "Thiruvananthapuram Assembly constituency") While the [Nadars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadar_(caste) "Nadar (caste)") are Concentrated on [Neyyattinkara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neyyattinkara_Assembly_constituency "Neyyattinkara Assembly constituency"),[Parassala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parassala_Assembly_constituency "Parassala Assembly constituency"),[Kovalam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kovalam_Assembly_constituency "Kovalam Assembly constituency").

As per the voter list published by the Election commission for the 2019 Lok Sabha elections, there were 13,34,665 voters in the electorate and 1077 polling stations in this constituency.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-ceo.kerala.gov.in-6) The voter turnout for the 2019 Lok Sabha election was 73.45% where as it was 68.63% and 65.74% in the 2014 and 2009 elections respectively.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram_Lok_Sabha_constituency#cite_note-7)

# Three-time MP Shashi Tharoor files nomination again from Thiruvananthapuram for Lok Sabha polls
## Senior CPI leader and former Thiruvananthapuram MP Pannian Raveendran and BJP leader and Union Minister Rajeev Chandrasekhar are Tharoor's challengers in the fray
With senior CPI leader and former Thiruvananthapuram MP Pannian Raveendran and BJP leader and Union Minister Rajeev Chandrasekhar as Tharoor's challengers in the fray, the high-profile Thiruvananthapuram constituency is set for a fierce three-cornered battle in the crucial polls this time.
Tharoor, who is a former UN diplomat, began his journey in electoral politics, winning the Thiruvananthapuram seat in the 2009 Lok Sabha polls.

The **Padmanabhaswamy Temple** (Malayalam:[[pɐd̪mɐnaːbʰɐswaːmi]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Malayalam "Help:IPA/Malayalam")) is a [Hindu temple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu_temple "Hindu temple") dedicated to [Vishnu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishnu "Vishnu") in [Thiruvananthapuram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiruvananthapuram "Thiruvananthapuram"), [Keralam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerala "Kerala"), India. It is one of the 108 [Divya Desams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Desam "Divya Desam") which are considered the sacred sites of the [Sri Vaishnava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sri_Vaishnavism "Sri Vaishnavism") tradition.

The temple's principal deity is [Anantha Padmanabhaswamy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anantha_Padmanabhaswamy?action=edit&redlink=1 "Anantha Padmanabhaswamy (page does not exist)"), a form of Vishnu depicted in [yogic sleep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoga-nidra "Yoga-nidra"), on his serpent mount named [Shesha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shesha "Shesha"). Padmanabhaswamy is the [tutelary deity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tutelary_deity "Tutelary deity") of the [Travancore royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore_royal_family "Travancore royal family"). The titular [Maharaja of Travancore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharaja_of_Travancore "Maharaja of Travancore"), [Moolam Thirunal Rama Varma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moolam_Thirunal_Rama_Varma "Moolam Thirunal Rama Varma"), is the current trustee of the temple.

### Past Temple management
The temple and its assets belong to the deity Lord Padmanabhaswamy, and for a long time, have been controlled by a trust headed by the [Travancore royal family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Travancore_royal_family "Travancore royal family"). The temple has six hitherto known vaults (nilavaras), labelled as A to F, for bookkeeping purpose by the Court (Since then, however, an Amicus Curiae Report by [Gopal Subramanium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gopal_Subramanium "Gopal Subramanium"), in April 2014, mentions two more subterranean vaults that have been labelled G and H).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmanabhaswamy_Temple#cite_note-ACR14Part01-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmanabhaswamy_Temple#cite_note-ACR14Part02-38) While Vault B is believed to be unopened since the 1880s, Vault A was possibly opened in recent decades, Vaults C to F have been opened from time to time over recent years.

I’m privileged and blessed to get to this opportunity to offer my prayers and seek blessings at the great Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple situated in Thiruvananthapuram, the capital of Kerela. “Thiruvananthapuram” in Malayalam translates to the City of Lord Anantha or the City of Lord Vishnu referring to the diety of Padmanabhaswamy temple.The temple is considered as the richest place of worship in the world.Padmanabhaswamy is the tutelary deity of the royal family of Travancore and the titular Maharaja of Travancore, namely Moolam Thirunal Rama Varma is the current trustee of the Temple.
